subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Alice / Raj —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to walk through your current retrieval + ranking flow. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain / goals
- Latency: customer-facing search needs sub-200ms median per query for top-K reranking (current stack ~600-800ms).
- Cost: embeddings and rerank are driving monthly spend; want clear levers to reduce unit cost.
- Reliability & SLOs: want graceful degradation and regional failover for EU traffic.
- Integration: minimal SDK surface changes preferred; prefer function-calling style for tool integration and structured outputs for downstream parsing.

What we discussed for fit / approach
- Embeddings + reranking: recommend hybrid approach — precompute embeddings for candidates, use lightweight semantic filtering + Redwood reranker for final scoring.
- Streaming & structured output: we’ll use streaming responses for the reranker to surface partial scores and a final JSON payload (structured output) to the service.
- Function calling: embed a function-calling wrapper in your API gateway so logs and observability remain centralized; Redwood SDK supports the same pattern.
- SDK changes: 1) small client update to invoke streaming/rerank endpoints, 2) optional client-side batching for request aggregation — no model architecture changes.
- Security / deployment: Redwood Dedicated or Private can be scoped if you need VPC/on-prem later; initial pilot can run on Hosted in us-west.

Attachments
- I’m attaching a short proposal and an integration diagram showing where the SDK and function-calling wrapper live.
[Attachment: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: integration-diagram.png (PNG)]

Next steps / asks
1) I’ll put together a one-week pilot plan (P0 metrics: median latency, tokens/cost delta, rerank precision on your eval set).
2) Marcus (cc’d) will scope the minimal SDK changes and share a short integration checklist.
3) If you want procurement looped in, please share the contact and timeline — we can include a ballpark pricing sheet in the pilot SOW.

Can you confirm the pilot success criteria above and whether procurement should be looped in now?

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid recap, appreciate it. A couple quick clarifying items from our side:

1) Quantization / model footprint: our infra team asked whether Redwood’s hosted reranker supports int8/quantized variants or if that’s only available on Dedicated/Private. We’re trying to understand the tradeoff for latency vs. accuracy.
2) Compliance / deployment: Acme will ultimately need a VPC deployment for PCI-scope workloads. For the pilot we can start on Hosted, but procurement wants confirmation that we can move to Private (on-prem or VPC) within 3 months of pilot completion if things look good.
3) Pricing: can you share a ballpark monthly cost for the pilot (estimate tokens + embeddings + rerank calls) — we don’t need exact numbers yet, just to flag to finance.

Also looping in Raj (cc) — he’ll track procurement/questions. If you can include a short tech note on quantization options and a statement about migration timelines to Private, that’d be great.

Best,
Alice

--
Alice Johnson
Director of Search & Relevance, Acme Corp
alice.johnson@acme.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Alice — copying the short tech note you requested. High level answers below and a recommended pilot scope.

Quantization / model footprint
- Hosted (Redwood API): we provide quantized variants for many open models in our catalog; for the reranker we typically recommend an 8-bit variant where available — that gives ~2-3x memory reduction with minimal accuracy loss for reranking tasks.
- Dedicated / Private: full control over quantization profiles and custom kernels; if you need the absolute lowest latency and deterministic throughput, Dedicated/Private is the path.

Migration / Private timeline
- Pilot on Hosted: 2–4 weeks.
- Private migration (VPC onboarding or on-prem package): typically 6–10 weeks after contract signature (shorter if you want a dedicated onboarding sprint and infra readiness).

Pilot cost ballpark
- For a 4-week pilot scoped at 50k queries/day with precomputed embeddings and 5 rerank calls per query, rough estimate: $6k–$12k (depends on model and streaming enabled). We’ll refine after we confirm model choices and batching.

Recommended pilot scope (deliverables)
- Week 0: confirm eval set + success metrics (latency median target: <=200ms; rerank precision delta >= +7% over baseline).
- Week 1–2: integration of Redwood SDK (streaming + function-calling wrapper) + sample rerank endpoint.
- Week 3: run traffic to pilot and collect metrics.
- Week 4: results review and decision on Dedicated/Private.

Action items I’ll take
- Share a short integration checklist (client update, streaming endpoint example, function calling example).
- Provide a quantization note with model-specific tradeoffs (will attach in a follow-up).

Marissa — I can jump on a 30m technical sync with Raj/Alice early next week if that helps.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
